answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before bidding; the same funds cannot back two active accounts. Calling accounts mesa, pigment, and prism changes nothing: three bidders require $300 locked at once. Every extra fake identity therefore costs an attacker another $100 in tied-up capital, plus its financing cost for the lock period. This limits cheap identity multiplication without claiming to prove who owns each agent.
